proof:
# Every feasible mass and base first moment is realized by one actual cap

Let C be a compact convex body in R^n x R^d and let its nonempty mixed
intersection have intrinsic dimension q>=1. Put

    mu=H_q restricted to S,
    P={z:dim C_z=q}, K_z=C_z, w_z=H_q(K_z)>0,
    v_z=(1,z) in R^(n+1),
    Z={sum_z t_z v_z:0<=t_z<=w_z}.                    (1)

Thus Z is the finite zonotope of feasible total masses and integer-base
first moments of dominated submeasures `0<=eta<=mu`. Lower-dimensional
fibers have zero mu mass and do not enter (1).

Choose ANY continuous direction u whose restriction to the direction space
of every K_z, z in P, is nonzero. Such a direction exists: finitely many
proper linear subspaces of R^d cannot cover R^d. In the full-volume case
q=d, every nonzero u is allowed.

For EVERY r in Z there exists theta=(b,a) in R x R^n such that the single
closed ambient halfspace

    H={ (z,x): b+a.z+u.x>=0 }                         (2)

has mass/base moment exactly

    (mu(H), integral_H z dmu)=r.                     (3)

The same prescribed u works for every r; no continuous-direction choice
depending on r is necessary. The normal in (2) is nonzero because u is
nonzero. All boundaries in (2) have zero intrinsic mu measure.

## 1. Feasible moments and the hinge potential

A dominated submeasure has masses t_z in [0,w_z], giving (1). Conversely
each such list is realized by density t_z/w_z on K_z, so (1) is the exact
feasible set, with no convex-body constraint imposed at this stage.

Define the convex function

    Psi(theta)=sum_z integral_(K_z)(theta.v_z+u.x)_+ dH_q(x).

It is continuously differentiable and

    gradient Psi(theta)=sum_z v_z
        H_q{ x in K_z:theta.v_z+u.x>=0 }.             (4)

Indeed u is nonconstant on every intrinsic affine span, so the threshold
hyperplane has zero H_q measure. Difference quotients of the hinge are
bounded by the corresponding fixed coordinate of v_z and converge except
on that null hyperplane. Dominated convergence proves differentiability
and continuity of the displayed gradient. Its values belong to
U=span{v_z}.

The support function of Z is

    h_Z(theta)=sum_z w_z(theta.v_z)_+.

The scalar hinge is 1-Lipschitz, hence

    |Psi(theta)-h_Z(theta)|
        <= sum_z integral_(K_z)|u.x| dH_q(x)=A<infinity.  (5)

This uniform bounded-error estimate supplies the required coercivity.

## 2. Targets in the relative interior

Suppose r belongs to relint Z. Since Z spans U and contains zero, its
affine hull is U. A relative ball `r+epsilon B_U` lies in Z for some
epsilon>0. Therefore for theta in U,

    h_Z(theta)-theta.r>=epsilon|theta|.

By (5), `Psi(theta)-theta.r` tends to infinity as |theta| tends to infinity
within U. It attains a minimum there. At any minimizer theta, the gradient
of this objective restricted to U is zero. Both (4) and r lie in U, so
this is the full vector equality `gradient Psi(theta)=r`. Equation (4)
then proves (3).

This argument allows linear dependence of the base coordinates and does
not presume that Z is full dimensional in R^(n+1).

## 3. Boundary targets and finite saturation

Now let r lie on the relative boundary of Z. Let F be the smallest face
of Z containing r, so r belongs to relint F. Because Z is a polytope,
there is a vector e exposing exactly F, that is,

    F={zeta in Z:e.zeta=h_Z(e)}.

One elementary justification is to intersect the finitely many facet
faces containing F and add their exposing functionals with positive
coefficients. Equality in the sum forces equality in each facet
inequality, hence exposes exactly their intersection F. Functionals are
taken in U; a redundant ambient orthogonal component is irrelevant.

Maximization over the independent segments in (1) gives the exact face
formula

    F=r_fixed+Z_0,
    r_fixed=sum_(e.v_z>0) w_z v_z,
    Z_0=sum_(e.v_z=0)[0,w_z]v_z.                      (6)

Every positive-sign fiber is forced full, every negative-sign fiber
forced empty, and only zero-sign fibers remain free. Thus
`r_0=r-r_fixed` belongs to relint Z_0.

Apply Section 2 to the zero-sign fibers in their own linear span, obtaining
a vector theta_0 with their cap moments exactly r_0. If there are no such
fibers, take theta_0=0. Extend theta_0 to R^(n+1) if necessary and put

    theta=T e+theta_0.

For zero-sign indices the cap expression is unchanged. For every other
index, the compact fiber bounds `theta_0.v_z+u.x` uniformly, while
`T e.v_z` has a fixed nonzero sign. One sufficiently large FINITE T
therefore makes every positive-sign fiber wholly contained and every
negative-sign fiber strictly excluded. The resulting single cap has
moments r_fixed+r_0=r. There is no limiting cap, boundary trace selection,
or possible loss of positive fiber mass in this step.

This also covers the extreme targets r=0 and r=sum_z w_z v_z.

## 4. Convex subbodies and exact integer centroid membership

If the first coordinate t of r is positive, D=C intersect H is itself a
convex body, and its intrinsic mixed measure is exactly `mu restricted to H`.
To see nonempty ambient interior, positive q-volume in a source fiber
cannot lie only on the cap boundary, by the choice of u. Thus C contains
a point strictly inside H. Interior points of the full ambient body C
approximate that point, and eventually remain strictly inside H.
Consequently D has nonempty interior. Its mixed intersection has intrinsic
dimension q: it has a retained q-volume piece and is contained in the
original source, whose integer fibers have no dimension exceeding q.

If r=(t,tj) for an integer j, the TRUE unweighted intrinsic centroid of
D intersect Lambda has base j. Its full barycenter belongs to D by compact
convexity and hence belongs to the required mixed set. In fact K_j in D
has positive q-volume: take the positive-volume retained source pieces
with their positive mass weights; their Minkowski average lies in D_j,
and has dimension at least q, hence exactly q. No exponential reweighting
is substituted for this actual cap-subbody centroid.

In particular define

    T_j=max {sum_z t_z:0<=t_z<=w_z,
                         sum_z (z-j)t_z=0}.           (7)

Whenever j is an integer with T_j>0, the maximum is attained by compactness
of the finite box. Sections 1--3 show that it is attained by ONE actual
cap-cut convex subbody with true integer-base centroid j. Conversely every
convex subbody, and indeed every dominated submeasure, with that centroid
has mass at most T_j. Thus (7) is an exact geometric retained-mass optimum,
not only a relaxed upper bound.

For reference, finite linear-programming duality gives

    T_j=inf_a sum_z w_z(1+a.(z-j))_+.                 (8)

Weak duality follows immediately by multiplying the balanced moment
constraint into `sum t_z`; equality is the usual finite box-constrained LP
duality. No attainment of this dual is needed for the geometric realization
or for (7). In particular any explicit a in (8) is a certified upper bound.

## 5. Scope and the counting boundary

The theorem applies to arbitrary n and to all positive intrinsic dimensions,
including different q-dimensional fiber direction spaces. It uses a generic
continuous functional, not a common intrinsic identification of those
spaces. It does not assert a depth bound at the retained centroid, a retained
fraction of 2^-n, or selection of a favorable integer j.

The q=0 restriction is essential. For example C=[0,1] in a pure integer
coordinate has two counting atoms, so its moment zonotope contains targets
of noninteger total mass that no halfspace restriction can realize. The
continuous threshold differentiability used above is absent in that case.
